sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Special Provisions for Divyang Students** refers to educational, legislative, and infrastructural adaptations designed for children with special needs (CWSN).

Evident from constitutional mandates (**Article 21A**, **Article 45**), legislative enactments (**PWD Act 1995**, **RPWD Act 2016**), and educational policies (**NPE 1986**, **RPWD Act 2016**, **NEP 2020**).
Applies to **Divyangjan** (differently-abled students) categorized under **21 specified disabilities** as per the RPWD Act 2016.
Ensures **Inclusive Education**, equal opportunity, non-discrimination, and mainstreaming of marginalized learners in accordance with **Right to Education (RTE) Act 2009**.
Provision of **Assistive Devices**, barrier-free architecture, **Special Educators**, curriculum adaptation, and flexible examination schemes.
Locomotor Disability, Visual Impairment, Hearing Impairment, Mental Retardation, Autism Spectrum Disorder, Learning Disabilities, and Multiple Disabilities.
Critical for **UP Assistant Teacher (Child Psychology)** exam under inclusive pedagogy, barrier-free learning, and special provisions.
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Education, **RCI (Rehabilitation Council of India)**, and NCERT.

items.title: Concept of Inclusive Education vs. Special Education
items.content:
• **Special Education:** Segregated schooling model specifically tailored for a particular type of disability.
• **Integrated Education:** Placing children with disabilities in mainstream schools with minimal structural adjustments.
• **Inclusive Education:** Systemic reform ensuring all children learn together in regular classrooms with necessary support services and universal design.
• **Normalization Principle:** Making available to all disabled persons patterns of life and conditions of everyday living which are as close as possible to regular circumstances.

items.title: Legislative Framework in India (Mnemonic: 'PRP-20') **Mnemonic: P-R-P**
items.content:
• **P - PWD Act 1995:** Persons with Disabilities Act focusing on non-discrimination, equal protection, and 3% job reservation.
• **R - RCI Act 1992:** Rehabilitation Council of India regulating training policies for professionals dealing with Divyangs.
• **P - PwD Rights Act 2016:** Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act expanding disabilities from **7 to 21 types** and increasing job reservation to 4%.
• **Mnemonic:** **'P**lease **R**ead **P**rovisions **20** times' for PWD 1995, RCI 1992, RPWD 2016.

items.title: Universal Design for Learning (UDL) Framework
items.content:
• **Principle 1 (Engagement):** Providing multiple means of engagement (the 'why' of learning).
• **Principle 2 (Representation):** Providing multiple means of representation (the 'what' of learning).
• **Principle 3 (Action & Expression):** Providing multiple means of action and expression (the 'how' of learning).
• **Goal:** Eliminating educational barriers at the design stage rather than retrofitting accommodations.

items.title: Assistive Technology and Adaptive Devices
items.content:
• **Visual Impairment:** **Braille displays**, screen readers (NVDA, JAWS), magnifiers, and talking calculators.
• **Hearing Impairment:** **Hearing aids**, cochlear implants, FM systems, and sign language interpreters.
• **Locomotor Disability:** Wheelchairs, crutches, artificial limbs, and adapted desks.
• **Learning Disability:** Audiobooks, speech-to-text software, graphic organizers, and colored overlays.

items.title: Psychological and Social Aspects of Divyang Students
items.content:
• **Self-Efficacy (Bandura):** Building belief in personal capability despite physical or cognitive challenges.
• **Social Constructivism (Vygotsky):** Emphasizing peer interaction, scaffolding, and More Knowledgeable Other (MKO) support in inclusive settings.
• **Stigmatization & Labelling:** Avoiding negative peer attitudes through sensitisation programs and cooperative learning.
• **IEP (Individualized Education Program):** Tailored instructional plans designed to meet the unique needs of a specific Divyang student.

items.title: Pedagogical Adaptations for Classroom Instruction
items.content:
• **Curriculum Modification:** Adjusting depth, breadth, and complexity of learning content.
• **Instructional Adaptation:** Using multisensory approaches (visual, auditory, kinesthetic/tactile - **VAK model**).
• **Assessment Accommodation:** Extra time, scribe assistance, large print question papers, and alternative testing formats.
• **Classroom Environment:** Seating arrangements near the board, acoustic control, and well-lit pathways.

items.definition: Remember sequence of major acts: **R**CI (**1992**), **P**WD (**1995**), **N**ational Trust (**1999**), **R**PWD (**2016**). Mnemonic: **R**aj **P**lays **N**ew **R**ound.
Remember **A-B-C-D**: **A**ccessibility (physical/digital), **B**elonging (social acceptance), **C**urriculum (flexible adaptation), **D**iverse support (assistive technology).

items.term: Trick 3: VAK Approach for Multi-sensory Teaching
items.definition: Use **V**isual (see), **A**uditory (hear), **K**inesthetic (touch/move). Essential for teaching children with sensory or learning challenges.
PWD 1995 had **3%** reservation -> RPWD 2016 increased job reservation to **4%** and higher education admission reservation to **5%**.
**A**ssessment of current level -> **P**lanning goals -> **I**mplementation of strategies -> **E**valuation of progress. Essential cycle for Individualized Education Program.
The old PWD Act 1995 recognized only **7** disabilities, whereas the modern RPWD Act 2016 expanded them to **21** specified disabilities.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Integrated with Inclusive Education
items.definition: Students often treat them as synonyms. **Integrated education** just places the child in a regular school without changing the system, while **inclusive education** transforms the school environment, curriculum, and teaching methods for all.

items.term: Mistake 2: Mixing up PWD Act 1995 and RPWD Act 2016 Reservations
items.definition: Remember that PWD Act 1995 had **3%** job reservation, whereas RPWD Act 2016 increased it to **4%** in government jobs and **5%** in higher education institutions.

items.term: Mistake 3: Believing Special Education is Segregated Only
items.definition: While traditional special education is segregated, modern special education acts as a **resource support system** within inclusive setups, providing itinerant teachers and resource rooms.

items.term: Mistake 4: Misinterpreting the Number of Disabilities in RPWD Act
items.definition: Do not write 7 or 19. The correct number of specified disabilities under the **RPWD Act 2016** is **21**.

items.term: Mistake 5: Assuming Divyang Students Only Need Physical Ramps
items.definition: Physical accessibility is vital, but psychological, curricular, technological, and communication accessibility (like **Braille** and **Sign Language**) are equally crucial.

items.term: Mistake 6: Confusing RCI with NCTE Mandates
items.definition: **RCI (Rehabilitation Council of India)** regulates training programs for special educators and rehabilitation professionals, whereas **NCTE** regulates general teacher education.
The term **Divyang** ('divine limbs') was introduced to replace the term 'Viklang' (disabled), promoting dignity and positive self-image.
**Article 21A** ensures free and compulsory education, and **Article 45** mandates early childhood care, applicable equally to Divyang children.
Recognizes **21 disabilities**, guarantees non-discrimination, equality of opportunity, and barrier-free accessibility in public buildings.
Includes children with disabilities aged **6 to 14 years** in neighborhood schools under mainstream inclusive education.
Framework focusing on multiple means of **engagement, representation, and expression** to cater to diverse learners.
A customized educational plan tailored to address the unique learning needs and goals of an individual CWSN.
Use of **Braille**, screen readers, hearing aids, wheelchairs, and adaptive software to bridge learning gaps.
Acts as a collaborator, resource person, and co-teacher in regular classrooms to support inclusive pedagogy.
Provision of **extra time (20 minutes per hour)**, scribes, compensatory marks, and alternate questions for visually or learning impaired students.
Envisions robust support for CWSN from foundational stage with resource centers and barrier-free infrastructure.
Statutory body established in **1992** to regulate and standardize training of special educators and professionals.

upscNotes.content: For the UP Assistant Teacher exam, focus heavily on the distinction between Integrated and Inclusive Education, and memorize the exact number of disabilities (21) under the RPWD Act 2016.
Questions frequently test examination concessions for Divyang students, such as extra time allocation (20 minutes per hour) and exemption from third language.
Trap: Examiners often mix up the reservation percentages between the old PWD Act 1995 (3%) and the RPWD Act 2016 (4% jobs, 5% higher education). Read the question carefully!
Trap: Do not assume that 'Inclusive Education' applies only to physical disabilities. It encompasses cognitive, sensory, social, and economic diversities as well.

keyTakeaways: RPWD Act 2016 recognizes **21 specified disabilities** and mandates 4% job reservation.
**Inclusive Education** adapts the school system to the child, unlike segregated special education.
**UDL (Universal Design for Learning)** relies on multiple means of engagement, representation, and expression.
**IEP (Individualized Education Program)** is essential for tailoring instruction to CWSN.
**RCI Act 1992** regulates special education and rehabilitation professionals in India.
Examination accommodations include extra time, scribes, and alternative assessment formats.
